arxiv-2401-11286.title: Data repairing and resolution enhancement using data-driven modal decomposition and deep learning Journal: XXX
arxiv-2401-11286.creator: Ashton Hetherington, Daniel Serfaty Bayón, Adrián Corrochano, Julio Soria, Soledad Le Clainche
arxiv-2401-11286.description: Abstract This paper introduces a new series of methods which combine modal decomposition algorithms, such as singular value decomposition and high-order singular value decomposition, and deep learning architectures to repair, enhance, and increase the quality and precision of numerical and experimental data.

arxiv-2410-20774.title: Are LLM-Judges Robust to Expressions of Uncertainty? Investigating the effect of Epistemic Markers on LLM-based Evaluation
arxiv-2410-20774.creator: Dongryeol Lee, Yerin Hwang, Yongil Kim, Joonsuk Park, Kyomin Jung
arxiv-2410-20774.description: Abstract In line with the principle of honesty, there has been a growing effort to train large language models (LLMs) to generate outputs containing epistemic markers . However, evaluation in the presence of epistemic markers has been largely overlooked, raising a critical question: Could the use of epistemic markers in LLM-generated outputs lead to unintended negative consequences?

arxiv-2601-18760.title: Beyond Preferences: Learning Alignment Principles Grounded in Human Reasons and Values
arxiv-2601-18760.creator: Henry Bell, Lara Neubauer da Costa Schertel, Bochu Ding, Brandon Fain
arxiv-2601-18760.description: Abstract A crucial consideration when developing and deploying Large Language Models (LLMs) is the human values to which these models are aligned. In the constitutional framework of alignment models are aligned to a set of principles (the constitution) specified in natural language. However, it is unclear how to fairly determine this constitution with widespread stakeholder input.

pmc-11592873.title: Basic Cells Special Features and Their Influence on Global Transport Properties of Long Periodic Structures
pmc-11592873.creator: Luna R N Oliveira, Marcos G E da Luz, Eric J Heller, Micheline Soley
pmc-11592873.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). In this contribution, we address quantum transport in long periodic arrays whose basic cells, localized potentials U(x), display certain particular features. We investigate under which conditions these “local” special characteristics can influence the tunneling behavior through the full structure. As the building blocks, we consider two types of U(x)s: combinations of either Pöschl–Teller, U0/cosh2[αx], potentials (for which the reflection and transmission coefficients are known analytically) or Gaussian-shaped potentials.

pmc-13027685.title: Prognostic Value of Systemic Inflammation Markers (NLR and Haemoglobin) in Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer: Survival Analysis from a Real-World Single-Centre Cohort Study
pmc-13027685.creator: Carina Maria Golban, Lavinia Davidescu, Alexandru Alexandru, Silviu Vlad, Alina Gabriela Negru, Sorin Saftescu, Petrescu Codruta Ileana, Catalin Prodan Barbulescu, Serban Mircea Negru
pmc-13027685.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background and Objectives: In real-world NSCLC management, prognostic assessment extends beyond tumour staging and molecular profiling, which represent a partial timeframe of disease biology. Routinely collected inflammatory and haematological markers may better reflect the dynamic host–tumour interactions during treatment. This study assessed the prognostic significance of baseline and longitudinal neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) and haemoglobin levels on survival outcomes in a real-world NSCLC cohort.

pmc-13401920.title: Integrating the Wei–Qi–Ying–Blood Theory with Modern Pathophysiology: A Multitarget Translational Framework for Dengue Management
pmc-13401920.creator: Tingni Wang, Xiqiao Li, Xiaoying Wang, Qin Li
pmc-13401920.description: Despite the substantial global burden of dengue, clinical management remains largely supportive. Severe disease involves viral replication, dysregulated inflammation, endothelial injury, plasma leakage, thrombocytopenia, and coagulation abnormalities. In this review, we link the traditional Chinese medicine Wei–Qi–Ying–Blood theory with stage-specific dengue pathophysiology and biomarker-guided risk assessment.
